Modals for Expressing Necessity, Duty and Advice
You use modals to express necessity, duty and advice. These are especially useful in a workplace setting.

You use the modal must to express obligation, or a duty. The speaker has decided that something must be done.

You must submit your work by next week.
I must submit my work by next week. (I have decided)

You can also use the modal have to to express an obligation or a duty.

I have to complete this article by next week.
You have to complete this article by next week

You use the modals should/ought to to express strong advice or duty to do something.

You should work hard to finish this work by next week. (advice)
You ought to finish this work by next week. (it's your duty)

You use need to refer to things that are necessary. You use the infinitive after the verb need.
You need to finish the work by next week.

How to Write a Job Post

A job post is a posting (online or in print) that an employer writes to attract new employees to an available position at their company. If you were to write a job post on behalf of your employer, these are some things to keep in mind.

The Title: This is most of the name of the position (Junior Editor)

Company Information: Include a blurb about what the company is and what they have to offer. Making the company stand out from others will attract a variety of applicants.

Qualifications: List the necessary qualifications and experience that you would like your candidates to have. Specify the skills and attributes they must possess.

Duties: Be specific about what the position involves. That way, you can be sure you are reaching all the best qualified candidates.

Make sure you leave sufficient contact information and/or be clear about how you want the candidates to send their application.
